findings.claim: enterRace arms the 330 ms overlay-removal timer (via playScreenChange) before the synchronous game.startRace(). startRace builds the world and the Three.js scene and renders the first frame (shader compile), and the CSS sweep cannot start until that work ends. On a slow phone the chequer band is therefore cut short, or removed before it is ever painted (first RACE of a session, NEXT RACE onto another track).
findings.suggestedFix: In enterRace call game.startRace({ trackId, carCount: PLAYER_CAR_COUNT }) first and playScreenChange(root, 'chequer') after it. Both land in the same painted frame, and the 330 ms timer then starts after the synchronous start work. AC8's expectSweep still passes.

findings.claim: The track radiogroup's keydown handler moves the selection and calls preventDefault() for every ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, including with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held. src/input/keyboard.ts:41 deliberately ignores those events so browser shortcuts (Alt+Left, Cmd+Left = Back; Cmd+Up/Down = scroll) keep working; here they are swallowed and change the track instead.
findings.evidence: src/ui/start-screen.ts:56-62: group.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { const step = { ArrowRight: 1, ArrowDown: 1, ArrowLeft: -1, ArrowUp: -1 }[e.key]; ... if (step === undefined || i < 0) return; e.preventDefault(); ... pick(next.id, true); }) has no modifier check. Repro: focus the first card, dispatch new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'ArrowLeft', altKey: true, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }) on it. Result: the selection wraps to the last card and the event is defaultPrevented, so the browser's Alt+Left Back never runs. Expected: ignored, as in keyboard.ts:41 `if (k.ctrlKey || k.metaKey || k.altKey) return;` (covered by tests/input/keyboard.test.ts:45).
findings.suggestedFix: At the top of the keydown handler add `if (e.altKey || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) return;`, the same guard as src/input/keyboard.ts:41.

findings.claim: The screen-change--stripes stage builds the real start screen without a bestLaps store, so its cards read the browser's real localStorage. A Stage must be deterministic (stage.ts:11), and start.stage.ts and raceStage (which only passes a trackId together with an in-memory store) avoid real storage.
findings.evidence: screen-change.stage.ts:10: createStartScreen(menuLayer(root), { onRace: () => {}, tracks: stageTrackCards() }).show(); -> start-screen.ts:32 `opts.bestLaps ?? localBestLaps`, and refreshBests() (called in show()) reads racer.bestLap.<id>. Repro (happy-dom): localStorage.setItem('racer.bestLap.bends', '40370'), render STAGES 'screen-change--stripes': the first card reads 'BEST 0:40.37' instead of 'BEST –:––.––', so the same stage renders differently depending on browser storage. The 1440x900 screenshot of this stage shows dashes only because harness/screens/capture.ts renders every stage before it plays any race in the same browser context (races write bests via race-ui). Opening the stage page in a profile with saved bests shows other content.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass `bestLaps: memoryBestLaps()` (or the `bests()` store used in start.stage.ts) in the stripes stage's createStartScreen options.
